info.description:
Public, read-only JSON API of **The Grid**, the S.I.E.R.R.A. data service. It gathers hazard and situational-awareness feeds for California's central Sierra Nevada, centred on Calaveras and Tuolumne counties: the Highway 4 / Ebbetts Pass corridor (Angels Camp, Murphys, Arnold, Dorrington, Bear Valley) and the Highway 49/108 towns (Sonora, Columbia, Twain Harte). Neighbouring counties (Alpine, Amador, El Dorado, Mariposa, San Joaquin, Stanislaus) are in the place directory because hazards cross county lines.

Upstream sources: CAL FIRE and FIRIS (wildfires and perimeters), Cal OES / Genasys (evacuation zones), the National Weather Service (alerts, fire weather, forecasts), USGS (earthquakes), CHP and Caltrans (incidents, lane closures, chain control, cameras, message signs), PG&E (outages and Public Safety Power Shutoffs), county burn lines and CAL FIRE burn permits, the MeshCore community radio mesh, Google Routes and OpenWeatherMap.

This service is an aggregator, not an authority. For a life-safety decision, link the official source. An event's link is `canonicalUrl` (the item's own page), else `provenance.sourceUrl`, else the `homepageUrl` of its source (`GET /api/v1/sources`, joined on `provenance.sourceId`). Either event field can be an empty string: CHP incidents, Caltrans lane closures, FIRIS perimeters and NWS alerts have neither, so their link is the source homepage. Every map feature carries `properties.source`, and evacuation views link Genasys (`metadata.sourceUrl`, `summary.evacuationSourceUrl`).

## Resource model

- **Event**: one item from one upstream source, such as a fire, an evacuation zone, a weather alert, a road incident, an outage, a mesh radio node or a county's burn status. The id is stable (`{source}:{native id}`, e.g. `chp:261106ST0341`) and every change is kept as a numbered revision.
- **Layer**: the event taxonomy (`Event.layer`). The *event layers* are stored and queryable at `/api/v1/events`: WILDFIRE, EVACUATION, WEATHER_ALERT, EARTHQUAKE, ROAD_INCIDENT, POWER, MESH and BURN_STATUS. The *condition layers* (`road_segment`, `chain_control`, `fire_weather`, `message_sign`) are live projections of current state, not events: they appear only on the `.geojson` map layers, in `GET /api/v1/conditions`, and in the place summary's domains.
- **Place**: a named geography (AREA, COUNTY, TOWN, CORRIDOR). Events attach to places geometrically and every event lists its `placeIds`.
- **Source**: an upstream feed with live health (`GET /api/v1/sources`).
- **PlaceSummary**: the one-call rollup for a place (mode, per-domain status, top events, evacuation count).

## Quickstart: build a dashboard for a place

1. Pick a place: `GET /api/v1/places` lists them all (about 20). For a dashboard use an AREA (`ebbetts-pass`), a COUNTY (`calaveras-county`) or a CORRIDOR (`hwy4-arnold-bearvalley`): those have a footprint, so events and conditions attach to them. Do not build a dashboard on a TOWN (`arnold`). A town is a point, so an event attaches to it only when the event's polygon covers it (an evacuation zone, a fire perimeter), a wildfire comes near, or the fact is county-wide (burn status). Point events (road incidents, outages, earthquakes) and road conditions never attach, so a town's summary can read QUIET with an open `roads` domain while its highway is closed. Use a town to label a location and to find its county (`parentId`), or map a point or an address with `GET /api/v1/places:resolve?lat=38.25&lng=-120.35` (or `?address=...`) and pick the most specific non-town place it returns. Use the `slug` in paths.
2. Headline status: `GET /api/v1/places/{slug}/summary` returns `mode` (QUIET, WATCH or ACTIVE), one block per domain (fire, evacuation, weather, roads, seismic, power, burn, comms), the top five hazards and `activeEvacuations`. Show each domain's `status` and `highestSeverity` next to `mode`: road and chain-control conditions (a closed highway) raise the `roads` domain but never `mode`.
3. Event feed: `GET /api/v1/events?place={slug}&status=ACTIVE&severityMin=MINOR`. Then `GET /api/v1/events/{id}` for detail and `/api/v1/events/{id}/history` for its timeline.
4. Map: `GET /api/v1/places/{slug}/map/{layer}.geojson` serves one RFC 7946 FeatureCollection per layer (documented separately from the RPCs below).
5. Context: `GET /api/v1/conditions?place={slug}` for current weather, forecasts and the fire-weather state, `GET /api/v1/cameras?place={slug}` for traffic cameras, and `GET /api/v1/sources` for source-health badges.

Poll every 30 to 60 seconds. JSON responses are cacheable for 30 seconds (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=30`), GeoJSON layers and mesh links for 60; upstream feeds refresh every 2 to 15 minutes.

## Filter the event feed

An unscoped `GET /api/v1/events` is mostly MESH nodes: hundreds of community radio nodes across Northern California, all INFO, many outside every place. It also holds a week of planned Caltrans roadwork (ROAD_INCIDENT, status SCHEDULED). For a hazard feed, pass `place`, pass `status=ACTIVE`, and either pass `severityMin=MINOR` or list the layers you want. POWER events at INFO are single-customer outages.

## Conventions

- **JSON field names are camelCase.** Every field is present, except the per-layer detail blocks on an event (only the one matching `layer` is sent), so the spec lists every other field in its schema's `required`. Only a field the spec marks `nullable` can be `null`: an object, timestamp or wrapper the server can leave unset, such as `geometry`, `expires` or `lastSuccessAt`. Everything else is never `null`. Objects and timestamps the server always fills (`provenance`, `ingestedAt`, `summary`, ...) are not marked nullable. An unset scalar is `0`, `""` or `false`. Arrays are `[]` and maps `{}` when empty. Wrapper-typed fields (`activeEvacuations`, the mesh gauges) are `null` when unknown, so a real `0` is never confused with "no reading".
- **Enums serialize as their name strings** (`"SEVERE"`), never as numbers.
- **Timestamps** are RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-11-07T03:13:00Z`), with up to nanosecond fractions.
- **64-bit integers are JSON strings** (protobuf JSON mapping): mesh counters such as `uptimeSeconds: "98350"` and `cadenceSeconds: "1831"`. Parse them; 32-bit integers are plain numbers.
- **Geometry: pass `geometryFormat=OBJECT`.** By default (`BASE64`, the legacy form kept for existing clients) `geometry.geojson` is a protobuf `bytes` field, so the RFC 7946 geometry JSON arrives base64-encoded: `JSON.parse(atob(event.geometry.geojson))`. With `geometryFormat=OBJECT` (on every route that returns events, revisions or places) the same geometry is a plain JSON object in `geometry.object` and `geometry.geojson` is empty. Coordinates are `[longitude, latitude]`. `geometry.bbox` and `geometry.centroid` are plain numbers in both forms. For maps, the `.geojson` layer endpoints serve whole FeatureCollections directly.
- **Query parameters**: this spec names them in camelCase (`severityMin`, `pageSize`, `pageToken`, `enhancementIo`). The snake_case forms (`severity_min`, `page_size`, ...) work too. Enum values are case-insensitive. A repeated parameter can be repeated (`layer=WILDFIRE&layer=POWER`) or comma-separated (`layer=WILDFIRE,POWER`).
- **Place addressing**: anywhere a place is named, the slug (`arnold`) or the namespaced id (`town:arnold`) works.
- **Pagination** is keyset-based. `pageSize` is a MAXIMUM: 0 or omitted means 50, values over 200 are clamped to 200, and a negative value is a 400. A page also stops before its encoded size passes about 3 MiB, so a page of perimeter-heavy events (fires, evacuation zones, outage areas) can hold fewer than `pageSize`; an event larger than that on its own is served alone on its page. Pass `nextPageToken` back as `pageToken` with the same filters (and the same `geometryFormat`) until it comes back empty: an empty token is the only end-of-list signal, never a short page. Tokens are opaque. Pages stay stable while new events arrive.
- **Conditional GET**: event lists, event detail, event history, the revision archive, places and cameras return a weak `ETag`. Send it back in `If-None-Match` to get `304 Not Modified`. The tag changes whenever the body would, including in-place refreshes that write no revision (AI text, mesh telemetry, burn-line observations, place re-attachment). The summary, conditions, sources, resolve, scanners and mesh-telemetry endpoints do not yet send ETags.
- **No authentication, no API key.** CORS is open (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`), GET only, no credentials, so a browser page on any origin can call the API directly.
- **Errors** are the gRPC status as JSON, `{code, codeName, message, details}`, with a mapped HTTP status: 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (bad enum, timestamp or page token, `geometryFormat`), 404 `NOT_FOUND` (unknown place, event or address), 503 `UNAVAILABLE` (address geocoder down, or a request interrupted by a deploy), 500 `INTERNAL`. Branch on `codeName`. During a deploy handoff any route can briefly answer `503`: the RPCs with the JSON error (`UNAVAILABLE`), the hand-built routes (`.geojson`, mesh links) with a plain-text body and `Retry-After: 1`. Retry after a second; a retried page request with the same `pageToken` resumes exactly where it was.

## Severity and status

Every event and map feature uses one severity scale: INFO (rank 0), MINOR (1), MODERATE (2), SEVERE (3), EXTREME (4). It expresses how urgently the public should respond, not physical magnitude. `severityRank` is the same value as a number, for sorting and colour ramps. `/api/v1/events` sorts by severity, then most recently observed.

Status lifecycle: SCHEDULED (planned, not yet in effect) → ACTIVE → RESOLVED (the authoritative feed stopped listing it) or EXPIRED (it aged out). An event that reappears goes back to ACTIVE with a new revision. The end of an event is a revision too, so history keeps the all-clear.

## Fail-loud honesty

The API never turns a failure into an all-clear.

- Source health is `OK`, `STALE` (serving last-good data while the upstream fails) or `UNAVAILABLE` (nothing trustworthy to serve). It appears on `/api/v1/sources`, on each summary domain, in the summary's `sources` sidecar, on `/api/v1/cameras`, and in each map layer's `metadata.sourceStatus`. UNAVAILABLE with no items means *unknown*. Render it as "unknown, check the source", never as "none".
- Evacuations: `summary.activeEvacuations` is `null` when the evacuation source is UNAVAILABLE (unknown; send people to Genasys at `summary.evacuationSourceUrl`), `0` when a healthy fetch found no active zone ("none reported", not a guarantee), and `N` when zones are active.
- A failed fetch never resolves or expires events. They stay as they were and the source reads STALE.
- The fire-weather state comes only from issued NWS products. The API never infers a Red Flag Warning that NWS has not issued.

## Casing quirks (kept for compatibility)

- Layer names in responses (`Event.layer`, `summary.topEvents[].layer`) are UPPERCASE enum names (`ROAD_INCIDENT`). Map-layer path segments are lowercase slugs (`road_incident.geojson`). `?layer=` accepts either, plus the aliases `mesh_node` and `network` for MESH.
- `fireWeather.state` is lowercase: `normal`, `elevated` or `red-flag`.
- Burn-status enum values carry a prefix (`BURN_DAY_YES`, `CALFIRE_PERMIT_REQUIRED`, `BURN_PERMISSION_ALLOWED`).

API changes are listed, dated, in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sierragridteam/sierra-data/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

get.description:
In-service Caltrans CCTV cameras within 25 km of a coverage area, each with
a snapshot image URL and, where Caltrans publishes one, an HLS stream URL.
Links only: images and streams are served by Caltrans, never proxied. With
`place`, only cameras within 25 km of that place, nearest first. Cameras are
reference views, not events: nothing here is a hazard, and an empty list
means no camera nearby. Refreshed every 6 hours; check `sourceStatus`.
Supports ETag / If-None-Match.

parameters.description:
Only cameras within 25 km of this place (slug or id), nearest first.
Default: every camera near any coverage area.
parameters.name: place

Current conditions per weather location (OpenWeatherMap, refreshed every 15
minutes), a 48-hour NWS forecast per location, and the region's fire-weather
state. With `place`, only the weather locations inside the place's bounding
box (and their forecasts); `fireWeather` is region-wide either way. Weather
ALERTS are events (`/api/v1/events?layer=WEATHER_ALERT`); road conditions
are the `road_segment` and `chain_control` map layers.

parameters.description:
Only weather locations inside this place's bounding box (slug or id). Does
not filter `fireWeather`.

get.description:
The main event feed, from the grid event store. Defaults: status ACTIVE and
SCHEDULED, every layer, every place, every severity, up to 50 per page.

An unscoped query is dominated by MESH nodes (hundreds of INFO community
radio nodes, many outside every place) and SCHEDULED Caltrans roadwork. For
a hazard feed pass `place` and `status=ACTIVE`, and either
`severityMin=MINOR` or an explicit `layer` list. Use
`layer=ROAD_INCIDENT&place={corridor}` for a highway's incidents and
`layer=WEATHER_ALERT` for NWS alerts. Sorted by severity, then most recently
observed. A page holds at most `pageSize` events and stops early at about
3 MiB encoded, so follow `nextPageToken` until it is empty. Supports
ETag / If-None-Match.

**Text search.** `q` keeps only events whose text matches: headline,
location, summary, the source's description and incident log, typed facts
(incident type, cause, zone id), node names and public keys, and the
source's name. Every word is required; `"quoted words"` must appear
together; `-word` excludes; `OR` between terms starts an alternative.
Words are matched by stem ("flooded" finds "flooding") and a numbered
road in any spelling finds every spelling (`hwy 4`, `SR-4`, `state route
4`). With `q` the order is newest `observedAt` first, not severity, and
the response adds `totalMatches`, `counts`, a `matches` snippet per event
and `search` (how the query was read and what it covers). The other
filters still apply, including the status default: add `status` to search
ended events. No matches means no stored event's text matched, not that
nothing happened: collection began at `search.since`, and weather
readings and road conditions are not events. `counts=true` returns the
total and its breakdown without a text query.

parameters.description:
Only events attached to this place: slug (`arnold`) or namespaced id
(`town:arnold`). Omit for every place, including events outside all places.
parameters.name: place

parameters.description:
Only these layers. Repeat the parameter or comma-separate. Case-insensitive;
lowercase slugs (`road_incident`) and the aliases `mesh_node` and `network`
(for MESH) also work. FIRE_WEATHER, GAUGE, AIR_QUALITY and ANNOUNCEMENT are
accepted but no events carry them. Default: every layer.
parameters.name: layer

parameters.description:
Only these statuses. Repeat the parameter or comma-separate.
Case-insensitive. Default: ACTIVE and SCHEDULED. Pass `ACTIVE` alone to drop
planned roadwork; add RESOLVED and EXPIRED to include ended events.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description:
Only events at this severity or above. Case-insensitive. Default: no
minimum (same as INFO). `MINOR` drops mesh nodes, burn status and
single-customer outages.

parameters.description:
Only events whose `observedAt` is at or after this RFC 3339 time, e.g.

parameters.name: since

can hold FEWER events than this, because it also stops before its encoded
size passes about 3 MiB (perimeter-heavy events): keep requesting while
`nextPageToken` is non-empty, and never treat a short page as the end.

Include the AI model's full prompt and response (`enhancement.request` and

strings.

parameters.description:
How each event's `geometry` carries its GeoJSON. `BASE64` (default, the
legacy form): the base64 `geometry.geojson` string. `OBJECT`: a plain
JSON object in `geometry.object`, with `geometry.geojson` empty. `NONE`:
no shape at all, only `geometry.bbox` and `geometry.centroid`, for lists
that do not draw shapes. Fire perimeters, evacuation zones and outage
areas are most of a page's bytes, so NONE pages are much smaller and
faster; fetch one event for its shape. Case-insensitive; anything else is
a 400.
parameters.name: geometryFormat

parameters.description:
Text search: only events whose text matches. Words are all required;
`"quoted words"` are a phrase; `-word` excludes; `OR` separates
alternatives. Stems match and a numbered road matches in any spelling.
At most 200 bytes and 16 terms. Changes the order to newest first. See
the operation description.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description:
With `q`, treat its last word as still being typed: it also matches words
that begin with it (`floo` finds "flooded"), unless `q` ends in a space.
For search-as-you-type boxes. Leave it off for a finished question or a
count, where `deer` must not match "Deerfield". Default false.
parameters.name: qTyping

parameters.description:
Return `totalMatches` and `counts` (matching events by layer and
category) even without `q`. Always on with `q`. Default false.
parameters.name: counts

get.description:
Events about the same situation, each with the rule that matched, a
plain reason and a confidence: a fire's evacuation zones (named in the
Cal OES notes, or the nearest fire to a zone issued soon after it
started), outages PG&E attributes to it, shutoffs and road reports near
it; shutoffs, outages and road reports inside a wind, fire-weather or
winter storm product's area while it is in effect. Works from either
side: an evacuation lists its fire. Relations state what the sources say
or how events coincide, never a cause the sources do not state.

A monitored road (`road:{id}`) lists the events its status was read from
(`roadSegment.causes[].eventId`), and each of them lists the road
(`road-status-cause`, HIGH): the road closed by a CHP incident and that
incident. It follows the road's current causes, so the link ends when the
cause does; a cause whose event is not stored is not listed. The same
holds for the chain requirements on a road (`roadSegment.chains[].eventId`,
`road-chains`, HIGH): the road lists each stretch it is under, and the
stretch lists the roads it is on.

Mesh nodes relate differently, by structure, not by situation: along the
reads an operator-run monitor states (`mesh.telemetry.readVia`), whatever
the nodes' status. A gateway (a companion radio a monitor listens through)
lists the repeaters read through it and they list it
(`mesh-monitor-gateway`); repeaters read through the same gateway, and
gateways that read the same repeater, list each other
(`mesh-monitor-peer`). Nothing is followed further, so parts of the mesh
that share no gateway and no repeater share no relations, even under one
monitor. The nodes of a monitor that states no gateways (it reads them
all from one place; `mesh.telemetry.admin.reporterId`) are each other's
`mesh-monitor-peer`. A node no monitor reads has none, and
a mesh node is never related to a fire, outage or road report. For radio
links between nodes use `GET /api/v1/mesh/links`. Computed
at read time from the stored events (every status), so rules can change
without a migration. Related events carry no shapes (as
`geometryFormat=NONE`); fetch one for its geometry.

parameters.description: Event id, e.g. `calfire:e51208a8-ae10-49ef-b719-60ba424dda40`.
parameters.name: id

404.description: NOT_FOUND: no event has this id.

get.summary: List events related to one event.

get.description:
The dense numeric series behind an event whose layer has one, shaped for
a chart. The event's revisions record when its state changed; its samples
are the readings in between. Two layers have samples, each recorded
about every 15 minutes and kept 400 days: ROAD_SEGMENT (`road:{road id}`,
one per roads refresh, in `road`) and WEATHER (`weather:{location id}`,
one per successful read of the location's current weather, in
`weather`).

The answer is at most `maxPoints` points (default 500, at most 2000).
When the window holds no more samples than that, each point is one
sample and `bucketSeconds` is 0. Otherwise the samples are grouped into
buckets of `bucketSeconds`: the narrowest of 5, 15 and 30 minutes, 1, 2,
3, 6 and 12 hours and 1 day that fits (then whole days). Buckets are
aligned to the Unix epoch, so a bucket's start does not depend on the
window. `coverage` says what the window holds and `gaps` where the
series has holes, so a chart can break its line there instead of joining
across them.

A closed road has no travel time: a sample taken while the segment was
CLOSED carries `null` for travel time and delay, and is left out of a
bucket's figures.

A weather point's figures are as OpenWeatherMap reported them, to its
decimals; `GET /api/v1/conditions` serves the latest reading in whole
numbers. A figure the source did not report is `null`, not 0.

Default window: the 7 days before `to` (default now); windows over 400
days are clamped. Supports ETag / If-None-Match: the validator changes
when a sample lands in the window. The raw rows, one per refresh and
unbounded, remain at `GET /api/v1/roads/{road}/history`.

parameters.description: The event id, e.g. `road:hwy4-arnold-bearvalley` or `weather:bearvalley`.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Window start, RFC 3339, inclusive. Default: 7 days before `to`.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Window end, RFC 3339, exclusive. Default: now.
parameters.name: to
maxPoints

400.description: INVALID_ARGUMENT: `from` not before `to`, or `maxPoints` below 1 or not a number.

404.description: NOT_FOUND: no event has this id, or its layer keeps no samples.

get.description:
What happened and when, in time order, with each entry marked by whose
clock it is on. `SOURCE` entries are times the upstream stated: when CHP
took the report and each line of its log, when a fire started, when a
closure was planned and set up, when an alert takes effect and ends,
when a mesh node was last heard and when a monitor's reads of it moved
to a different gateway. `GRID` entries are when the Grid
recorded something: first stored, a status change (resolved, expired,
back again), a change to severity or a tracked figure (fire size and
containment, evacuation level, customers out). Use this instead of
inferring times from revision stamps. Built from the current event and up
to its 500 most recent revisions (`truncated` says when there were more).
Supports ETag / If-None-Match.

parameters.description: Event id, e.g. `chp:261106ST0341`.
parameters.name: id

404.description: NOT_FOUND: no event has this id.

get.description:
Revisions of all events, optionally filtered by place and layer, over a
half-open `[from, to)` window on each revision's `observedAt`. With no
window it covers all history. Ordered newest first. Place and layer
filters use each event's CURRENT place attachments and layer. Use it for
"what happened here last week". A page holds at most `pageSize` revisions
and stops early at about 3 MiB encoded, so follow `nextPageToken` until it
is empty. Supports ETag / If-None-Match.

**Text search.** `q` (same syntax as on `/api/v1/events`) keeps only
revisions whose text matched as it stood at that revision, so it finds
what a report once said and no longer says. Each revision gains a
`match` snippet and the response `totalMatches` and `search`. With
`collapse=event` the answer is one row per event in `collapsed` instead

Every undirected relay link observed within `window`, mesh-wide (not
place-scoped: a mesh spans places). Nodes are identified by public key;
to draw a link, join `a` and `b` to `properties.mesh.publicKey` on the
`mesh_node` map layer (or `mesh.publicKey` on `layer=MESH` events) for
coordinates. For a place-scoped, ready-to-draw version use the
`mesh_link` map layer. Weight edges by `daysActive`, fade by `lastSeen`.

**One node's links: `?node=`.** With `node` (a full public key) the
answer is only the links that end at that node, most recently seen
first, plus two members the whole list does not have: `node` (the key,
normalized) and `nodes`, which names every node the links mention
(name, type, status, the two activity clocks, position). This is "what
does this node hear". A key the Grid has no record of is a valid
question: its links are returned and it is simply absent from `nodes`.
An empty `links` means no link to the node was observed in the
window, which is common for a node whose traffic cannot be attributed
and is not evidence that it hears nothing: links are learned only from
packet paths the Grid could resolve without guessing.

`Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` and a weak `ETag` (`W/"…"`) that
excludes `generatedAt`: `If-None-Match` revalidates to `304` until the
links change.

get.description:
Is there a way across the mesh from one node to another, and through
which nodes. `from` and `to` are each one or more public keys (a side
is a set because a caller often means a place: "from Arnold" is
whichever node near Arnold has a way out), and the answer is the
cheapest route from any node of `from` to any node of `to` over the
links of `/api/v1/mesh/links` in the same `window`.

**It is an inference, and `basis` says so in every response.** The
links are learned only from packet paths the Grid could resolve
without guessing, so real links are missing: `found: false` means no
path was observed, not that none exists, and a path found is a chain
of links that each carried traffic in the window, not a promise that
a message sent now would be delivered. Show `basis` (or its sense)
with the route.

The route prefers fewer hops; a link last seen more than 24 hours
ago, or seen fewer than 3 times in the window, counts as half a hop
more each, so a route over fresh, busy links can beat a shorter one
over stale ones. Only repeaters and room servers (and relays the Grid
has no record of, which are in the links because they relayed) are
passed through; a companion or sensor can only be an end.
`alternate` is a second route that shares none of `path`'s relays (or,
when `path` is one direct link, does not use that link): `null` means
the observed links hold no such route, so each relay on `path` is a
single point of failure as far as the evidence goes. `linkCounts`
gives each requested node's number of links in the window: an end
with `0` is the usual reason a search fails.

`Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` and a weak `ETag` that excludes
`generatedAt`.

An RFC 7946 FeatureCollection of one layer's features within a place.
Coordinates are `[longitude, latitude]`. Check `metadata.sourceStatus`
before drawing: UNAVAILABLE means unknown (empty `features`), STALE
means last-good data.

| layer | features | backed by |
|---|---|---|
| `road_incident` | Points: CHP incidents (category `incident`) and Caltrans planned lane closures (`closure`, SCHEDULED until set up) | events |
| `chain_control` | Points: one per stretch of highway under R1/R2/R3 (at its low end, the signs listed in `chainControl.signs`), one per seasonal pass closure | live Caltrans |
| `road_segment` | LineStrings: configured routes with travel time; `status` OPEN/CLOSED/RESTRICTED/MAINTENANCE; the chain requirements on each in `road.chains` | live Google Routes + Caltrans |
| `message_sign` | Points: Caltrans message signs and their text; always INFO | live Caltrans |
| `weather_alert` | null geometry: NWS zone watches/warnings/advisories | events |
| `fire_weather` | one null-geometry region banner (`fw:region`) plus forecast Points | live NWS |
| `earthquake` | Points | events (USGS) |
| `wildfire` | Points or (Multi)Polygon perimeters | events (CAL FIRE, FIRIS) |
| `evacuation` | (Multi)Polygon zones; `status` is the level | events (Cal OES) |
| `power` | Polygons/Points: PG&E outages (`unplanned`/`planned`) and PSPS (`psps`) | events |
| `mesh_node` | Points: MeshCore nodes in the place; always INFO | events |
| `mesh_link` | LineString relay links touching the place plus the MESH_NODE Points at both ends (neighbours outside the place have `mesh.inRegion: false`); honours `window` | derived |
| `camera` | Points: Caltrans CCTV cameras near the place, nearest first; always INFO | live Caltrans |

Event-backed layers carry only ACTIVE and SCHEDULED features, and each
feature `id` is an event id usable with `/api/v1/events/{id}`. The
`.geojson` suffix is optional (`/map/wildfire` is the same resource).

**Caching.** `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` and a weak `ETag`
(`W/"…"`) over the layer's content, excluding `metadata.generatedAt`.
Revalidate with `If-None-Match`: the answer is `304` until the
features, `sourceStatus`, `lastSourceUpdate` or `attribution` change,
so polling a quiet layer costs no body.

Present and true when the stretch was put together from signs
lying within 15 km of each other, because the source lists
active signs only and nothing reports the road between them:
every Caltrans district we read through cc.kml alone (3 and 9),
and everything while the CWWP2 portal is down. `from` and
`to` are then the outermost signs reported, not a confirmed
continuous extent. Absent when Caltrans's
own signs, including the ones reading R-0, establish the
stretch.

level.description: Absent on a closure and on a truck or hold level.

seasonal.description: Present and true on a closure point that is a gate of a named seasonal closure (today the Ebbetts Pass winter closure on Highway 4): a closure that recurs every year at this place and is expected at this time of year. Show it as context, not as a hazard; its severity is INFO. Absent on every other feature, including closure points that are not a recognized gate.

signs.description: Every checkpoint Caltrans reported in the stretch, in order from `from` to `to`. Nothing Caltrans sent is dropped by the grouping.

MapChainPlace.description: One end of a chain-control stretch. `from` is the low end as California counts mileposts (west, or south); equal to `to` when the stretch is one place.

coordinates.description: `[lng, lat]` of the sign at this end.

place.description: The checkpoint's name, title-cased when Caltrans wrote it in capitals.

MapChainSign.description: One Caltrans chain-control checkpoint (one sign, one direction) inside a stretch, as reported.

id.description: The id this sign had as a feature of its own before 2026-11-14: `cc:{CWWP2 checkpoint index}` or `cc:{district}-{cc.kml message id}`.

postmile.description: CWWP2 signs only. Restarts at each county line.

since.description: When this sign entered its level.

MapClosureProps.description:
Set on Caltrans planned lane closures (category `closure`) only. One
feature per work window. `plannedEnd` is an estimate crews overrun: an
ACTIVE closure past it is still on the road until Caltrans records it
picked up.

lanesClosed.description: Caltrans's lane list, verbatim., example: "1, 2, LShoulder, RShoulder"

setUpAt.description: When the crew reported the closure set up. Absent while SCHEDULED.

MapEvacuationProps.description: evacuation block (Cal OES / Genasys zones). Life-safety; reference only, link `source.url`.

MapFeatureCollection.description:
An RFC 7946 FeatureCollection for one place and one layer. `metadata` is
an RFC 7946 §6.1 foreign member that map libraries ignore; read it for
source health and attribution before drawing.

features.description: Possibly empty. Empty with `sourceStatus` OK means confirmed-empty; empty with UNAVAILABLE means unknown.

MapFeatureProperties.description:
The envelope shared by every feature of every layer, plus exactly one
per-kind block named after the layer (`incident`, `road`,
`chainControl`, `messageSign`, `weather`, `fireWeather`, `earthquake`,
`wildfire`, `evacuation`, `power`, `mesh`, `meshLink`, `camera`).
Optional members are omitted, never `""` or `0`, when they have no value.

areaLabel.description: Where, in words ("SR 4 at Country Club Drive", "Murphys, CA").

description.description:
Longer text. road_incident: the readable narrative (AI-enhanced for
CHP, composed from Caltrans fields for closures). evacuation: Cal OES
public info, verbatim, never paraphrase. weather_alert: the NWS text,
verbatim. road_segment: why a road is not OPEN.

effective.description: When it began or takes effect (a SCHEDULED feature's start).

expires.description: Upstream expiry (weather alerts, fire-weather products). Not set from PG&E restoration estimates.

headline.description: One-line label for a popup or list row.

id.description:
Stable feature id. On event-backed layers it IS the event id, so
`GET /api/v1/events/{id}` returns the full record and its history
(`wildfire`, `evacuation`, `weather_alert`, `earthquake`,
`road_incident`, `power`, `mesh_node`). Condition layers use their
own ids (`road:…`, `cc:…`, `cms:…`, `fw:…`, `mesh_link:…`, `d10-…`).
A chain-control stretch is `cc:{route}:{level}` (`cc:hwy4:r2`),
which holds while the stretch grows or shrinks by a checkpoint.

kind.description: Human label for the feature type.

layer.description:
UPPERCASE layer of THIS feature. Usually the URL layer upper-cased,
except that the `mesh_link` layer mixes `MESH_LINK` edges and
`MESH_NODE` points. Only some values equal an Event `layer` enum
(`v1Layer`): WILDFIRE, EVACUATION, WEATHER_ALERT, EARTHQUAKE,
ROAD_INCIDENT and POWER do. MESH_NODE is the Event layer `MESH`.
ROAD_SEGMENT, CHAIN_CONTROL, MESSAGE_SIGN, MESH_LINK and CAMERA are
map-only. FIRE_WEATHER exists in the enum but these features are
conditions, not events.

severity.description:
Unified severity. `message_sign`, `camera`, `mesh_node`, `mesh_link`
and fire-weather forecast points are always `INFO` (context, not
hazards). Most power outages are INFO too: the median outage affects
one customer.

severityRank.description: Numeric severity for sorting and styling: INFO 0, MINOR 1, MODERATE 2, SEVERE 3, EXTREME 4.

status.description:
Meaning depends on the layer, and it is NOT always the Event
`EventStatus`:
- wildfire, weather_alert, earthquake, road_incident, power,
  mesh_node: the lifecycle `ACTIVE` or `SCHEDULED` (an advance watch,
  a planned closure window not yet set up, a planned shutoff). Map
  layers never carry RESOLVED or EXPIRED features; those are in
  `/api/v1/history`.
- evacuation: the evacuation LEVEL `ORDER` | `WARNING` | `ADVISORY` |
  `SHELTER_IN_PLACE`.
- road_segment: the road status `OPEN` | `CLOSED` | `RESTRICTED` |
  `MAINTENANCE` (absent until the road has been measured).
- absent on chain_control, message_sign, fire_weather, camera and
  mesh_link edges.

subhead.description: What is particular to this event among events with the same headline (same as Event.subhead), e.g. the elevation band of one of several NWS alerts for one storm. Today only on `weather_alert`. Absent when the event has none.

summary.description: AI-written plain-language summary (same as Event.summary). Absent when the event has none; fall back to `description`.

summaryEnhanced.description: Present with `summary` when a model wrote it, so a UI can label it as machine-written.

updatedAt.description: Last content revision. For mesh nodes this is NOT liveness; use mesh.lastHeardAt / lastRelayedAt.

MapFeatureSource.description: The upstream feed this feature came from. Render `attribution` with the feature.

id.description:
The upstream's id. Values today: `calfire`, `firis`, `caloes`,
`nws`, `usgs`, `chp`, `caltrans`, `google`, `pge`, `psps`,
`meshcore`. On the event-backed layers (`wildfire`,
`evacuation`, `weather_alert`, `earthquake`, `road_incident`,
`power`, `mesh_node`) it is the event's `provenance.sourceId` and
has a row in `GET /api/v1/sources` whose `status` is that feed's
health.

The condition layers (`road_segment`, `chain_control`,
`message_sign`, `fire_weather`), and `camera` and `mesh_link`, are
fetched or computed on request, outside the ingest scheduler that
writes the registry. `google` (on `road_segment`) has no registry
row at all. `caltrans` and `nws` do have rows, but those track the
scheduled lane-closure and alert polls, not the live fetch behind
these layers. For these layers judge health by the layer's
`metadata.sourceStatus` (the summary's `roads` and `fire` domains
fold the same statuses in), never by a missing or unrelated
registry row.

url.description: Deep link to the upstream record or viewer, when there is one.

MapFireWeatherProps.description:
fire_weather block. The region banner (id `fw:region`, null geometry)
carries the ISSUED `state`; only NWS products set it (Fire Weather Watch
-> elevated, Red Flag Warning -> red-flag). Forecast points (id
`fw:forecast:<location>`) carry `forecast` instead, are always INFO and
never imply a warning.

sourceEvent.description: The NWS product behind the state, e.g. Red Flag Warning.

MapGeometry.description:
An RFC 7946 geometry, or `null` for a feature with no location (NWS zone
alerts and the fire-weather region banner): render those as a banner
or list row, not a shape.

A position is `[longitude, latitude]`, longitude FIRST (RFC 7946
§3.1.1), the reverse of the `{lat, lng}` objects on the JSON RPCs.
Store-derived positions are trimmed to 5 decimals (~1 m).

Which types appear: Point (most layers: incidents, signs, cameras,
chain controls, quakes, mesh nodes, forecast points, unmapped fires);
LineString (road_segment routes, mesh_link edges); Polygon or
MultiPolygon (power outage areas, evacuation zones, fire perimeters).
Geometry passed through from an upstream ArcGIS feed may be any RFC 7946
type except GeometryCollection.

logNumber.description: CHP log number, or the Caltrans closure id.

MapLayerMetadata.description: Provenance and freshness of the whole layer.

area.description: Slug of the requested place (even when it was requested by id).

attribution.description: Credit line to render with the layer whenever it is drawn. Parts are joined with " · ".

generatedAt.description: When this body was rendered. Not part of the ETag.

lastSourceUpdate.description: Last successful upstream fetch. Present only when `sourceStatus` is not OK and a success is on record.

layer.description: The lowercase layer slug from the URL (not the UPPERCASE `properties.layer`).

schemaVersion.description: Envelope schema version; bumps only on a breaking envelope change.

sourceStatus.description:
Health of the feeds behind this layer, the fail-loud contract:
`OK` - current and complete. `STALE` - upstream is failing (or one
of two feeds is); these features are the last good data, as of
`lastSourceUpdate`. Show them with a caveat. `UNAVAILABLE` - nothing
trustworthy to show; `features` is always empty and the layer's
state is UNKNOWN. Never render it as "no hazards".

sourceUrl.description: The authoritative viewer for the layer, where one exists. Always set on `evacuation` (Genasys Protect), in every state.

MapMeshAdminProps.description: The last sample an operator monitor read off the node itself. Gauges the device did not report are absent, never 0.

MapMeshLinkProps.description: mesh_link edge block - one undirected relay link between two located nodes. Weight by `daysActive`/`observations`, fade by `lastSeen`.

a.description: Public key of one end (a < b).

b.description: Public key of the other end.

bestSnr.description: Peak SNR of an advert over the link. Absent when 0.

daysActive.description: Distinct days the link was observed.

observations.description: Packets seen traversing the link in the window.

MapMeshProps.description:
mesh_node block (MeshCore node presence; also on the MESH_NODE points of
the mesh_link layer). Signal readings are absent when no bridge heard the
node; a present 0 is a reading. A node's freshness is the later of
`lastHeardAt` and `lastRelayedAt`, never the feature's `updatedAt`.

gateways.description: Public keys of the observers that heard the node.

hopCount.description: Hops on the last heard path. 0 = heard direct.

inRegion.description: mesh_link layer only: true = inside the requested place, false = a neighbour outside it, included because it links in.

lastHeardAt.description: When the node's own signed advert last reached the Grid.

lastRelayedAt.description: When a packet this node relayed last reached the Grid.

publicKey.description: 64-hex Ed25519 public key; joins to MeshLink a/b.

reachability.description: An operator monitor's verdict on the node's admin interface. Absent when no monitor watches it.

MapMessageSignProps.description: message_sign block - what a Caltrans changeable message sign is showing, verbatim. Context, not a hazard.

pages.description: One or two pages of exactly three lines; a blank line is "". Absent when the sign is blank or unreadable.

route.description: The route Caltrans files the sign under. Where routes run together this is one of them.

routes.description: Every route the sign is on when that is more than `route` - the filed route first, then the one in the sign's name. Absent otherwise.

MapPowerProps.description:
power block, both PG&E feeds. `category` unplanned|planned sets the
outage fields; `psps` (Public Safety Power Shutoff) sets the PSPS fields.
`estimatedRestoration`, `deEnergizationEnd` and `allClear` are PG&E
ESTIMATES that are routinely overrun; label them as estimates.

allClear.description: PG&E's PLANNED all-clear, not proof the shutoff ended.

cause.description: Raw PG&E cause code, often blank.

medicalBaselineAffected.description: Customers whose medical equipment depends on grid power.

MapRoadProps.description: road_segment block (Google Routes travel time over a configured route). The numbers are absent, not 0, until the route has been measured.

beyond.description: Named seasonal closures past one of the segment's ends that are in effect now, such as the Ebbetts Pass winter closure past Bear Valley. They do not change the segment's `status` or `severity`: the segment is as open as `status` says. An entry appears only when Caltrans words the closure as the configured span; any other closure naming those places closes the segment. Absent when there are none. A seasonal closure is INFO, so it is not counted or listed in the place summary's roads domain.

from.description: Where it starts, in the source's words.
from.example: 0.5 mi east of the Jct of SR 207 /Mt Reba Turnoff/

headline.description: One line that names the closure without calling the segment closed.
headline.example: Hwy 4: Ebbetts Pass winter closure (past Bear Valley) — snow

reason.description: snow, ice, winter_closure, seasonal_closure, construction, rockslide, mudslide, fire, flooding, accident. Absent when the text gives none.

seasonal.description: True for a closure that recurs every year at this place and is expected at this time of year. Show it as a standing condition, not as a hazard. Always true today.

severity.description: The closure's own severity. A seasonal closure is INFO. The segment's `severity` does not include it.

side.description: END - past the segment's destination (the last coordinate of its line); START - before its origin.

status.description: What the highway is past that end.

to.description: Where it ends, in the source's words.

chains.description:
The chain requirements on this road: one entry per chain-control
stretch (R1, R2 or R3) that lies on it, highest level first,
then by `eventId`. Closures and truck or hold levels are not
listed. Chains do not change the road: its `status`, `severity`
and `headline` are the same with or without them, so a road
under R2 is OPEN.

**Absent and empty are different answers.** Absent means not
known: Caltrans's chain-control data could not be read, came
from only one of its two sources, or has a sign on this highway
whose status or position could not be read; or the road has no
measured route yet (its line is the two-point fallback). Show
"unknown", not "none"; the `chain_control` layer says what is
known. `[]` means Caltrans reports no chain requirement on this
road.

A stretch is on the road when it is on the same highway and one
of its signs stands within 250 m of the road's line, or when
none does but its signs stand past both ends of the road. A
stretch that runs on past one end of the road and covers less
than 1 km of it is not on it (chains from just above a town are
not on the road that ends in the town). An entry is the whole stretch, not the part on this
road, so `from` and `to` can lie past the road's ends. It is the
`chain_control` feature with the same id, which lists the signs.
The two are read from Caltrans separately, each at most every 5
minutes, so one can show a change up to 5 minutes before the
other.

eventId.description: The stretch's id: the id of its `chain_control` feature, and of its event (`/api/v1/events/{id}`) when the stretch has a sign inside a coverage area.

from.description: The low end of the whole stretch (west, or south): `chainControl.from.place`.

headline.description: The stretch's headline, as on the `chain_control` layer.
headline.example: Hwy 4 chains required, Mill Creek to Mount Reba Road (R2)

inferred.description: The stretch's `chainControl.inferred`: true when it was put together from signs lying near each other and nothing reports the road between them. Always present.

since.description: When the stretch's earliest sign entered the level. Absent when no sign reports a time.

to.description: The high end of the whole stretch: `chainControl.to.place`. Equal to `from` when the stretch is one place.

delayMinutes.description: Minutes over free-flow. 0 is a real reading.

statusCauses.description: What set a non-OPEN status, so a client can draw the part of the segment each covers instead of painting all of it. Absent when OPEN.

end.description: [lng, lat]; only for a closure with an extent.

eventId.description: The matching /api/v1/events id when known (CHP incidents).

extent.description: SPAN - fromKm..toKm along the segment (a closure running past the segment is cut at its end); POINT - one place (fromKm = toKm); UNKNOWN - no position on the segment (text-only condition, or too far off the line).

fromKm.description: km along the segment from its configured origin.

source.description: road_condition is Caltrans highway-conditions text, which has no position.

sourceId.description: CHP log number or Caltrans closure id.

statusSince.description: When the segment entered its current status, from the Grid's own samples (GET /api/v1/roads/{road}/history). Absent until sampled.

statusSinceAtLeast.description: True when the status already held at the first sample the Grid has, so it began no later than statusSince.

typicalMinutes.description: Median travel time when OPEN over the last eight weeks, at this hour of the week (typicalBasis HOUR_OF_WEEK) or across all hours (ALL_HOURS) when that hour has too few samples. Absent until there are enough.

MapWeatherProps.description: weather_alert block. The NWS CAP fields are verbatim; `nwsSeverity` is NWS's own scale, distinct from the unified `severity`.

MapWildfireProps.description: wildfire block (CAL FIRE incidents and FIRIS perimeters).

hasPerimeter.description: True when the geometry is a mapped perimeter rather than a point.

MeshLink.description: One undirected relay link. Every member is always present.

a.description: Public key (64 hex) of one end; a < b.

b.description: Public key of the other end.

bestSnr.description: Peak SNR (dB) of an advert seen traversing it; 0 when none was measured.

daysActive.description: Distinct days observed; a reliability weight.

observations.description: Packets seen traversing the link in the window.

links.description: With `node`, most recently seen first; an empty list means none was observed in the window, not that the node hears nothing.

node.description: Only with `?node=`. The requested node's public key, lowercase, without the `meshcore:` prefix.

nodes.description:
Only with `?node=`. What the Grid knows about the nodes the links
mention, by public key. A key with no entry is a relay the Grid
has no record of (outside its area, or never heard advertising).

MeshNodeRef.description: A mesh node as a link or path names it. Every member is always present.

lastHeardAt.description: `mesh.telemetry.lastHeardAt`: when the node's own advert last reached the Grid. `null` when none is on record.

lastRelayedAt.description: `mesh.telemetry.lastRelayedAt`: when a packet the node relayed last reached the Grid. `null` when none is on record.

location.description: The advertised position. `null` for a node that shares none.

nodeType.description: Repeaters and room servers relay; companions and sensors do not.

status.description: The node event's status. EXPIRED: no advert or relay for its presence window; it can still end links seen earlier in the window.

MeshPacket.description: One reception. Extra bridge fields are accepted and ignored.

RSSI.description: Reception RSSI in dBm (number or numeric string).

SNR.description: Reception SNR in dB (number or numeric string).

origin_id.description: Receiving radio's public key, if different from `observer`.

packet_type.description: MeshCore payload type; only 4 (ADVERT) updates a node.

raw.description: The full over-the-air frame as hex (header, path, payload), or a meshcore://<hex> link.

timestamp.description: Ignored; the server stamps its own receive time.

MeshPacketReport.description:
`mesh.packet` (schema_version 1): raw MeshCore frames a companion radio
heard, in the per-packet envelope the MQTT bridges publish. ADVERTs
(packet_type 4) update a node after its Ed25519 signature verifies;
other flood-routed packets credit relays. Answers 400 when MeshCore
ingest is off on the server.

observer.description: Public key (or 4+ byte prefix) of the receiving radio. Defaults to the reporter id.

MeshPath.description: The result of a path search. Every member is always present; `path` and `alternate` are `null` when there is none.

alternate.description: A second route that shares none of `path`'s relays (or not its one link). `null` when the observed links hold none.

basis.description: What the answer rests on and cannot show. Show it, or its sense, with the route.

found.description: `false`: no chain of observed links joins the two sides. Not observed, never "no path".

linkCounts.description: Each requested node's number of links in the window.

nodes.description: The nodes `from`, `to` and the routes mention, by public key; a key with no entry is a relay the Grid has no record of.

id.description: Node public key or a prefix of it (8-64 hex). A bad id is a warning; the rest of the report still lands.

last_attempt.description: Unix seconds of the monitor's last attempt on this node.

last_success.description: Unix seconds of the last successful read; null if never. Reachability is derived from its age.

online.description: Accepted and logged, but not used; reachability comes from last_success.

MeshRepeaterReport.description:
`mesh.repeater` (schema_version 1): an operator monitor's COMPLETE
current set of MeshCore repeaters it logged into. A report replaces the
reporter's previous set; a node left out is no longer monitored. Request
bodies are snake_case. Unknown fields are ignored. Unread values are
`null`, never `0`.

generated_at.description: When the report was built. Clamped to the server's clock.

hops.description: Number of links; 0 when one node is on both sides.

links.description: The link between each neighbouring pair of `nodes`, in order (`hops` of them).

nodes.description: Public keys in order, origin first.

rpcStatus.description:
The error body of every JSON route: the RPCs (gRPC-Gateway rendering of
google.rpc.Status) and the hand-built GeoJSON, mesh-links and ingest
routes alike. Served with the HTTP status mapped from `code`
(3 INVALID_ARGUMENT -> 400, 5 NOT_FOUND -> 404, 13 INTERNAL -> 500,
14 UNAVAILABLE -> 503, ...). All four members are always present.

codeName.description:
Canonical gRPC code name for `code`, e.g. `NOT_FOUND`,
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `INTERNAL`. Branch on this rather than the
message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Not stable; do not parse.

v1BoundingBox.description: BoundingBox is a WGS 84 bounding box in decimal degrees.

minLng.description: Western edge, degrees longitude (negative in California).

v1BurnDay.description:
BurnDay is the county air district's call for today.

 - BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN: Not read, unreadable, or older than 36 hours. Never treat as permissive.
 - BURN_DAY_YES: Permissive burn day: burning allowed (subject to CAL FIRE's status).
 - BURN_DAY_NO: No-burn day: burning prohibited.
 - BURN_DAY_MARGINAL: Restricted or partial day (for example elevation limits). Treated as a
restriction, not a yes.

v1BurnLineReading.description: BurnLineReading is one recorded phone line's answer for today.

burnDay.description:
This line's own answer. BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN if not read or stale. A change
writes a revision.

observation.description:
The latest call: message, transcript, confidence and time. `null` when the
line has never been read. Changes daily without writing a revision.

phone.description: The number a resident can call, E.164.

v1BurnObservation.description:
BurnObservation is the latest reading of one burn line. The line's message
names the date, so it changes every day even when the answer does not; that
is why it writes no revision.

confidence.description:
The model's confidence in the reading, 0-100. Shown rather than
thresholded: this is an AI reading of phone audio, so show it when it is low.

message.description:
The line's answer in plain language, extracted by a model from the
transcript.
message.example: Today is a burn day with no elevation restrictions.

transcript.description: Cleaned machine transcript of the recording.

v1BurnPermission.description:
BurnPermission is the combined answer, deliberately pessimistic.

 - BURN_PERMISSION_UNKNOWN: At least one facet is unknown or stale and none prohibits: assume nothing.
 - BURN_PERMISSION_ALLOWED: Both facets are known and permit burning today.
 - BURN_PERMISSION_PROHIBITED: At least one facet prohibits burning today.

v1BurnStatusDetail.description:
BurnStatusDetail is the BURN_STATUS detail block: whether residential/outdoor
burning is allowed today in one county.

Two independent authorities must BOTH permit a burn, and each is a separate
facet because they fail independently: `burnDay`, the county air district's
daily permissive-burn-day call (read from its recorded phone line), and
`calfireStatus`, CAL FIRE's seasonal suspension of burn permits on State
Responsibility Area land (changes about twice a year). `permission` combines
them pessimistically.

The event exists for each tracked county at all times, is always INFO and
ACTIVE, and is left out of the summary's hazard rollup (it has its own `burn`
domain). `GET /api/v1/events/burn:{county slug}/history` shows when it changed.

burnDay.description:
The county line's answer for today, merged across `burnLines` taking the
most restrictive (any NO wins, then any MARGINAL; YES needs every dialed
line to answer). BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN when unread or the reading is older than
36 hours.

burnLines.description:
--- county facet (source `burnline`) ---
Every recorded phone line that speaks for this county, each with its own
reading. One line can serve several counties, and a county can have several
lines. A line we could not read still appears, with `burnDay`
BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN and its phone number, so a reader can call it.

calfireArea.description: Land classes CAL FIRE's status covers.

calfireEffective.description:
--- CAL FIRE facet (source `calfire-burn`) ---
When CAL FIRE's current status took effect (the county line only ever says
"until further notice"). `null` when CAL FIRE gives no date.

calfireObservedAt.description:
When CAL FIRE's page was last read successfully. The only way to tell that
`calfireStatus` is being carried forward rather than freshly confirmed. Can
be `null`.

calfireStatus.description:
CAL FIRE's permit status for the county's SRA land. Carried forward from the
last good read while CAL FIRE's page is unreachable; check
`calfireObservedAt`.

permission.description:
The answer to "may I burn today?": PROHIBITED if either facet prohibits
burning (no-burn day, marginal day, or CAL FIRE suspension); ALLOWED only
when both facets are known and permissive; otherwise UNKNOWN. A missing
answer never reads as ALLOWED.

v1CalfireBurnStatus.description:
CalfireBurnStatus is CAL FIRE's permit status for State Responsibility Area
land in the county.

 - CALFIRE_BURN_STATUS_UNKNOWN: Unknown: CAL FIRE's page has not been read.
 - CALFIRE_BURNING_SUSPENDED: Permits suspended: no residential burning.
 - CALFIRE_PERMIT_REQUIRED: Burning allowed with a valid CAL FIRE permit.
 - CALFIRE_NO_PERMIT_REQUIRED: Off-season: no permit needed.
 - CALFIRE_BURNING_ALLOWED: CAL FIRE's page says "Burning Allowed": it is not restricting burning in
the county, and the decision falls to the air district's burn-day call
(`burnDay`). Says nothing about permits.

v1Camera.description:
Camera is one Caltrans CCTV camera. Every listed camera is in service and has
an image; an out-of-service camera is dropped, not flagged.

description.description: Caltrans's note on the view, e.g. "Looking South". Usually an empty string.

direction.description: Direction the camera faces along the route. Empty string when not given.

distanceMeters.description:
Metres from the requested place, or, without `place`, from the nearest
coverage area. 0 means inside it.

imageRefreshMinutes.description: How often Caltrans replaces the snapshot, in minutes. 0 when not reported.

imageUrl.description: Current snapshot JPEG, hosted by Caltrans (cwwp2.dot.ca.gov).

streamUrl.description: HLS playlist (.m3u8) for live video. Empty string for an image-only camera.

cameras.description: Cameras, nearest first, then by id. Empty when none is nearby.

lastSourceUpdate.description: When the served list was fetched. `null` when `sourceStatus` is OK.

sourceStatus.description:
Health of the camera list. STALE: served from an older fetch, or a
configured district is missing. UNAVAILABLE: no list fetched yet, or no
camera districts configured.

v1ChainControlDetail.description:
ChainControlDetail is one stretch of highway under one chain requirement
(layer CHAIN_CONTROL, event id `cc:{route}:{level}`, e.g. `cc:hwy4:r2`; a
second stretch of the same level on one route is `cc:hwy88:r2:2`). Caltrans
reports chain controls sign by sign; the Grid groups the signs of one
requirement into a stretch.

The id names the requirement, not its signs: it holds while the stretch
grows or shrinks by a checkpoint (a revision), and a change of level
resolves this event and opens another. The id is reused: the next
requirement of the same level on the same route is this event again,
ACTIVE in a new revision, so one event's history is every such
requirement on that highway. A stretch that splits, merges or
gains a neighbour before it on the road renumbers, which reads as one event
resolving and another opening. The event's geometry is a point at the low
end (`from`); each sign's own position is in `signs`.

direction.description:
Direction of travel, only when every sign in the stretch faces the same
way. Empty string for a stretch signed in both directions.

from.description:
The stretch's two ends, low end first (west to east, south to north).
Equal when the stretch is one place.

highway.description: The highway as Caltrans names it.

inferred.description:
The stretch was put together from signs lying near each other, because
the source lists active signs only and nothing reports the road between
them (Caltrans Districts 3 and 9). False when Caltrans's own signs
establish it.

level.description:
The requirement: `R1` (chains or snow tires), `R2` (chains, except
four-wheel drive with snow tires) or `R3` (chains on every vehicle).

signs.description: Every checkpoint Caltrans reported in the stretch, `from` to `to`.

v1ChainControlPlace.description: ChainControlPlace is one end of a chain-control stretch.

location.description: Where the checkpoint is. `null` when Caltrans gave no position.

v1ChainControlSign.description: ChainControlSign is one Caltrans checkpoint inside a stretch, as reported.

county.description: County and postmile (CWWP2 only; empty strings otherwise).

direction.description: The direction of travel the sign faces.

id.description:
The sign's own id: `cc:{CWWP2 checkpoint index}` or
`cc:{district}-{cc.kml message id}`.

location.description: Where the sign is. `null` when Caltrans gave no position.

since.description: When Caltrans says the sign took this status. `null` when not given.

source.description: The host the entry came from (`cwwp2.dot.ca.gov` or `quickmap.dot.ca.gov`).

fireWeather.description:
The region's fire-weather state. Region-wide, whatever `place` was asked.
Can be `null` when the weather service has no fire-weather reading.

forecast.description:
Per-location forecasts, joined by `locationId`. Every location in
`locations` whose forecast is available, whether or not its current
`weather` could be read. A location whose forecast could not be fetched
is simply missing here.

lastUpdated.description: When the weather data was last refreshed.

locations.description:
The monitored towns (within `place`, when given), with position and
elevation, in configuration order.

weatherStatus.description:
Health of `weather` (OpenWeatherMap current conditions): OK; STALE when
the set, or any town's reading in it (`weather[].observedAt`), is older
than 1.5x its refresh interval (15 minutes); or UNAVAILABLE when it
could not be read at all, in which case `weather` is empty and
`lastUpdated` null.
Render UNAVAILABLE as "current conditions unknown", never as no towns.
`forecast` and `fireWeather` come from NWS and do not depend on it.

v1DailyForecastPeriod.description:
DailyForecastPeriod is one of NWS's named 12-hour forecast periods
("Tonight", "Wednesday") for a location's grid cell.

precipitationProbabilityPercent.description: Probability of precipitation, percent. `null` when NWS gave none.

shortForecast.description: NWS's short forecast, e.g. "Chance Rain Showers".

temperatureCelsius.description: The period's high (day) or low (night), degrees Celsius.

windDirection.description: Compass point the wind blows from, e.g. "SW".

windSpeed.description: NWS's wind text, e.g. "5 to 10 km/h".

v1EarthquakeDetail.description:
EarthquakeDetail is the EARTHQUAKE detail block. The USGS event page is the
envelope `canonicalUrl`.

felt.description: Number of USGS "Did You Feel It?" reports. 0 when none.

v1Enhancement.description:
Enhancement marks AI-generated text so a client can badge it. The model
translates and summarizes the upstream text; it never asserts new facts, and
the original stays in `description`.

fields.description:
Which Event fields the model wrote, by JSON name: any of `headline`,
`summary`, `subhead`, `severity`.

model.description: Model that produced the text, e.g. "gpt-5-mini".

request.description:
The incident-specific prompt sent to the model (the static system prompt is
not included). Empty string unless the request set `enhancementIo=true`.

response.description:
The raw structured JSON the model returned. Empty string unless the request
set `enhancementIo=true`.

v1EvacuationDetail.description: EvacuationDetail is the EVACUATION detail block, one Cal OES / Genasys zone.

county.description: County as Cal OES spells it (uppercase).

eventType.description: Upstream event type, often an empty string.

level.description:
Coded level. An unrecognized upstream status is coded WARNING, never
dropped. ORDER and WARNING and SHELTER_IN_PLACE put the place summary in
ACTIVE mode; ADVISORY puts it in WATCH.

zoneId.description: Genasys zone id. `provenance.sourceUrl` links the zone's Genasys page.

v1Event.description:
Event is one item from one upstream source: a hazard, or a piece of ambient
state such as a mesh node or a county's burn status.

The envelope fields are the same for every layer, so a client can render a
card from `headline`, `severity`, `status` and `provenance` without knowing the
layer. Layer-specific fields are in exactly one detail block (`wildfire`,
`evacuation`, `weatherAlert`, `earthquake`, `roadIncident`, `mesh`, `power` or
`burnStatus`), chosen by `layer`; the other blocks are absent. `fireWeather`
is never populated on an event.

areaLabel.description:
Human-readable location ("SR 4 at Country Club Drive", "Calaveras County").
Empty string when the source gives none.

burnStatus.description: BURN_STATUS detail (one county's residential burning status).

canonicalUrl.description:
Link to the authoritative page for THIS item: a USGS event page, a CAL FIRE
incident page, a mesh node's CoreScope page, PG&E's outage or PSPS page, the
CAL FIRE burn-permit page for burn status. Always http(s) when set. Empty
string when the source has no per-item page, which today means CHP
incidents, Caltrans lane closures, FIRIS perimeters, NWS alerts and
evacuation zones. Fall back to `provenance.sourceUrl`, then to the source's
`homepageUrl` (`GET /api/v1/sources`, joined on `provenance.sourceId`).

description.description:
Long-form original text from the upstream (CHP log, NWS product body,
evacuation instructions, closure description). May contain newlines. Empty
string when the source has none, or when it would only repeat the headline.

effective.description:
When the event took or takes effect: alert onset, incident start, outage
start, closure set-up time. `null` when the source does not say.

enhancement.description:
Present when an AI model generated some of this event's text; lists which
fields. `null` for events with no AI involvement.

expires.description:
The upstream's declared end, such as an NWS alert's expiry. `null` for most
layers. Restoration estimates and planned closure ends are never put here
(they are routinely overrun); they live in the detail blocks.

fireWeather.description:
Never populated on an event: fire weather is a condition
(`GET /api/v1/conditions`, the `fire_weather` map layer).

geometry.description:
Where the event is. `null` for events with no footprint of their own: NWS
zone alerts (they attach to places by zone instead) and burn status (a fact
about a county).

headline.description:
One-line, card-ready title. Present on every event. For CHP incidents it
may be AI-written (see `enhancement.fields`); for NWS alerts it is composed
from the product, never by AI.
headline.example: Traffic hazard causing near-miss incidents; CHP responding

id.description:
Stable event id, `{source}:{native id}`. It never changes over the event's
life, so it is safe as a client key. Namespaces: `calfire:`, `firis:`
(wildfire), `evac:` (evacuation zone), `wx:` (NWS alert), `usgs:`
(earthquake), `chp:` (CHP incident), `caltrans:` (Caltrans lane-closure
window), `pge:` (outage), `psps:` (power shutoff), `meshcore:` (mesh node),
`burn:` (county burn status), `weather:` (weather location). Ids can
contain colons; URL-encode them in a path.

ingestedAt.description: When the Grid stored this revision.

layer.description:
Which layer this event belongs to. It decides which detail block is
populated.

nature.description:
What kind of thing this event is, which follows from its `layer`:
something that happens (OCCURRENCE) or the standing state of something
the Grid tracks (STATE). Read this instead of keeping a list of layers:
a count of "events happening" is a count of OCCURRENCE events, and a
layer added later says which it is. Set on every event the API returns.

observedAt.description:
When the upstream last changed this event's content. It moves only when a
new revision is written, so it is NOT "last seen". For a mesh node's
liveness use `mesh.telemetry.lastHeardAt` / `lastRelayedAt`; for burn
status it follows each new phone-line reading.

placeIds.description:
Ids of every place this event attaches to, e.g. `["county:calaveras-county",
"town:arnold"]`. Point events attach to the polygon places that contain them
and to corridors within about 1.5 km. Polygon events attach to places they
overlap. Wildfires also attach to AREA and TOWN places within 20 km. Empty
when the event is outside every place (common for mesh nodes).

power.description: POWER detail (PG&E outage or Public Safety Power Shutoff).

provenance.description: Which source published it, with attribution text to display.

readings.description:
How many of this event's revisions are readings (`EventRevision.kind`
READING): a reading with content of its own arrived and the state held.
`revision - readings` is the number of changes, counting the first. 0 for
every layer that records no readings (today only BURN_STATUS does: one
per call to a burn line).

revision.description:
Revision number, starting at 1. It increases by one on every content change
or status transition. `/api/v1/events/{id}/history` lists every revision.

roadIncident.description: ROAD_INCIDENT detail (CHP incidents and Caltrans lane closures).

severity.description:
Unified severity, INFO..EXTREME. Response urgency, not magnitude. See the
Severity enum for how each layer is graded. `enhancement.fields` lists
`severity` when an AI model assessed it (CHP incidents).

status.description:
Lifecycle status. `/api/v1/events` returns ACTIVE and SCHEDULED unless you
ask for others.

subhead.description:
A short line saying what is particular to this event among events with the
same headline. Empty string when there is nothing to add. Show it beside
the headline wherever two such events can sit in one list. Today only NWS
alerts carry one: the weather service issues one product as several alerts
(one per elevation band, for example), and their headlines are identical.
For such an alert it is AI-written when `enhancement.fields` lists
`subhead` (at most 60 characters, built only from the alert's own text,
such as `1 to 3 ft above 5,000 ft`), and otherwise taken from the alert's
own zone names (`weatherAlert.areaDesc`, the zones the Grid covers; up to
160 characters). An alert with no other alert of the same product beside
it has none.

summary.description:
AI-written plain-language summary of two or three sentences, for CHP
incidents and NWS alerts. Empty string when none was generated. The original
text is always kept in `description`.
summary.example: Reported traffic hazard on SR 4 at Country Club Drive. CHP responded. No lanes reported blocked.

v1EventCount.description: EventCount is how many matching events share a layer and category.

category.description: The events' `category`, e.g. `incident` or `closure`; may be empty.

v1EventHistoryMatch.description:
EventHistoryMatch is one event's revisions that match a text query,
collapsed: when its text first matched, when it last did, how many did.

first.description:
The earliest matching revision (inside the `from`/`to` window, if any),
in full, with its `match` snippet.

lastRevision.description:
The latest matching revision's number. Equals `first.revision` when only
one matches. If it is below the event's current revision, the event's
text stopped matching after it.

matchingRevisions.description: How many of the event's revisions match.

v1EventList.description: EventList is one page of events.

counts.description:
`totalMatches` broken down by layer and category, ordered by layer then
category. Empty unless the request had `q` or `counts=true`.

events.description:
Events on this page, ordered by severity (highest first), then
`observedAt` (newest first), then id. With `q`: `observedAt` newest
first, then id.

matches.description:
With `q`: where the text matched, keyed by event id, for the events on
this page. An event that matched only on an identifier or its source's
name has an entry with no `parts`. Empty without `q`.

nextPageToken.description:
Token for the next page; pass it as `pageToken` with the same filters.
Empty string on the last page.

search.description:
With `q`: how the query was read and what the search covers. Null
without `q`.

totalMatches.description:
How many events match the filters (and `q`) across every page. Null
unless the request had `q` or `counts=true`.

v1EventNature.description:
EventNature says what kind of thing an event is. It follows from the layer.

 - EVENT_NATURE_UNSPECIFIED: Never returned.
 - OCCURRENCE: Something that begins and ends: a wildfire, an evacuation, a weather
alert, an earthquake, a road incident or closure window, a power outage,
a chain requirement. `status` is its lifecycle: ACTIVE or SCHEDULED
while it is on, RESOLVED or EXPIRED when it is over.
 - STATE: The standing state of something the Grid keeps track of: a mesh node, a
county's burn status, an upstream feed's health, a monitored road. The
event lasts as long as the thing does and is ACTIVE throughout; what is
going on is in its detail (a road that is CLOSED is an ACTIVE event whose
`roadSegment.status` is CLOSED), and its revisions are when that
changed. Not something happening: leave these out of counts of events,
and expect `severity` INFO for most of them.

v1EventRevision.description: EventRevision is one stored snapshot of an event.

event.description:
The full event as it was at this revision. Mesh activity clocks
(`lastHeardAt`, `lastRelayedAt`) are not filled on history snapshots.

ingestedAt.description: When the Grid stored this revision.

kind.description:
Why this revision was written: the state changed (CHANGE), or a reading
of an unchanged state arrived (READING). Never unspecified.

match.description:
On `/api/v1/history` with `q`: where this revision's text matched. Null
otherwise.

observedAt.description: The upstream content time of this revision (`event.observedAt`).

v1EventRevisionList.description: EventRevisionList is one page of revisions.

collapsed.description:
With `q` and `collapse=event`: one row per event with a matching
revision, ordered by the latest match (newest first), then event id.
`revisions` is empty in that case.

nextPageToken.description:
Token for the next page; pass it as `pageToken` with the same filters.
Empty string on the last page.

revisions.description:
Revisions on this page. Per-event history: newest revision first. The
archive (`/api/v1/history`): `observedAt` newest first, then event id, then
revision newest first.

search.description:
With `q`: how the query was read and what the search covers. Null
without `q`.

totalMatches.description:
On `/api/v1/history` with `q`: how many revisions match across every
page, or with `collapse=event` how many events. Null without `q`.

v1EventSamples.description:
EventSamples is one event's samples over a window. The envelope is the same
for every layer; the list that is filled depends on the event's layer.

bucketSeconds.description:
0 when each point is one sample. Otherwise the width of each bucket in
seconds: every point then stands for the samples in
[`at`, `at` + `bucketSeconds`) that are inside the window. Bucket starts
are multiples of `bucketSeconds` since the Unix epoch, so the first
point's `at` can be earlier than `from`, and the first and last buckets
hold only the part of them the window covers.

coverage.description: What the window holds, before any bucketing.

from.description: Window start actually used (after defaults and clamping).

gaps.description:
Stretches of the window without samples, oldest first: between two
consecutive samples further apart than three times the sampling
interval, from `from` to the first sample, and from the last sample to
`to` (or to now, when `to` is in the future). Found on the samples
themselves, before bucketing. A window with no samples at all is one
gap. Break a chart's line across each.

layer.description: The event's layer, which says which list below holds the points.

v1EventStatus.description:
EventStatus is an event's lifecycle state. Every transition is a revision, so
the history keeps when an event started and ended.

 - EVENT_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: Never returned.
 - SCHEDULED: Planned or forecast and not yet in effect, e.g. a Caltrans lane-closure
window the crew has not set up yet.
 - ACTIVE: In effect now.
 - RESOLVED: Over: an authoritatively active-only feed (CAL FIRE, Cal OES, CHP, Caltrans,
PG&E) stopped listing it after a successful poll, or a closure passed its
planned end plus an overrun grace without a pickup call.
 - EXPIRED: Aged out: past its own `expires`, or unseen for longer than the source's
grace (`Source.expireAfterSeconds`). Used where a feed going quiet proves
nothing (NWS alerts, FIRIS perimeters, mesh nodes).

entries.description:
Entries oldest first. At the same instant a SOURCE entry comes before a
GRID one (the world's event before the Grid's record of it). Planned and
estimated times can be in the future.

truncated.description:
True when the event has more than 500 revisions and only the most recent
500 were read: GRID change entries before them are missing, and
FIRST_RECORDED still comes from revision 1.

v1FireWeatherConditions.description:
FireWeatherConditions is the region's fire-weather state, from issued NWS
products only. It never claims a Red Flag Warning that NWS has not issued.

headline.description: The NWS product's headline. Empty string when the state is normal.

state.description:
LOWERCASE state: `normal`, `elevated` (a Fire Weather Watch is in effect)
or `red-flag` (a Red Flag Warning is in effect). Empty string when the
state could not be determined.

zones.description: NWS fire-weather zones under the product. Empty when normal.

v1FireWeatherDetail.description:
FireWeatherDetail is never populated on an event. Fire weather is a condition,
served by `GET /api/v1/conditions` (`fireWeather`) and the `fire_weather` map
layer.

state.description:
`normal`, `elevated` (Fire Weather Watch) or `red-flag` (Red Flag Warning).
Lowercase.

v1ForecastPeriod.description:
ForecastPeriod is one hour of a location's forecast (NWS gridpoint data),
rounded to whole numbers. A value NWS did not give is 0.

precipitationMm.description:
Liquid-equivalent precipitation in this hour, mm. NWS forecasts amounts
over spans (usually 6 hours); each hour carries an equal share, so sum the
hours for a total.

precipitationProbabilityPercent.description:
The fields below are `null` when NWS gave no value for the hour, never 0:
a forecast 0% chance of rain and no forecast are different statements.

Probability of precipitation, percent.

snowLevelMeters.description:
Snow level: the elevation above which precipitation falls as snow,
metres above sea level.

snowfallMm.description: Snowfall in this hour, mm of snow (not liquid), shared out the same way.

weather.description:
The forecast weather in words, from NWS's grid vocabulary, e.g. "Chance
of light rain showers"; several are joined with "; ". Empty when NWS
forecasts none.

windDirectionDegrees.description: Direction the wind blows FROM, degrees clockwise from north.

v1Geometry.description:
Geometry is an event's or place's footprint.

The GeoJSON comes in one of two forms, chosen per request with
`geometryFormat`: `BASE64` (the default and legacy form) fills `geojson`;
`OBJECT` fills `object` and leaves `geojson` empty. `bbox` and `centroid`
are the same in both.

bbox.description:
Bounding box of the geometry, in decimal degrees. Always set when geometry
is present.

centroid.description:
Representative point for markers and list views: the point itself for a
Point, otherwise the middle of the bounding box (which can fall outside an
irregular polygon).

geojson.description:
LEGACY FORM (the default, `geometryFormat=BASE64`). The RFC 7946 GeoJSON
geometry object (Point, LineString, Polygon, MultiPolygon, ...) as UTF-8
